title: Israeli Forces Arrest at Least 53 Palestinians in Biddu Raid Following Neve Tzuf Shooting
detail: Israeli forces raided the town of Biddu, northwest of occupied Jerusalem, at dawn on Monday, September 21, 2026 -- the third incursion into the town since a Palestinian resident was accused of shooting dead Israeli settler Netanel Shukrun at a spring near Neve Tzuf (Halamish) the previous day, on the eve of Yom Kippur. The Jerusalem Governorate said Israeli forces detained at least 53 young men, holding them at an interrogation and detention center set up inside a house seized during the raid, and that soldiers searched, vandalized and damaged several homes and physically assaulted residents. Biddu Mayor Nazmi Mansour said 'the occupation forces have abused and assaulted a number of citizens during ongoing raids.' An Al Jazeera correspondent said Israeli forces were conducting field interrogations 'to remind people that if anyone is considering an attack against Israelis, then the whole town ... will pay the price.' The Israeli military said the suspected gunman had fired on vehicles near Halamish before being shot, wounded and arrested at a Ramallah-area hospital hours after the shooting. The raid followed Prime Minister Netanyahu's instruction to security forces to increase their presence in the West Bank and carry out arrests and offensive operations after the Neve Tzuf shooting and a separate thwarted car-ramming attack near Ganim, Jenin, on September 20.

media.caption: Israeli soldiers arrest two Palestinians during a raid in the town of Biddu in the occupied West Bank, September 21, 2026

confidenceReason: The scale of the raid and detentions is corroborated by the Jerusalem Governorate (relayed via WAFA, Tier 1 Palestinian Authority news agency) and independently reported by Al Jazeera (Tier 2); the IDF's account of the preceding Neve Tzuf shooting is the military's own characterization.

title: 11-Year-Old Boy Among Four Palestinians Killed in Israeli Fire Across Gaza, Including in 'Safe Zone' of Al-Mawasi
detail: Israeli forces killed at least four Palestinians across the Gaza Strip on Monday, September 21, 2026, despite the nominal October 2025 ceasefire. In the al-Mawasi 'safe zone' in southern Gaza, 11-year-old Ismail al-Bardawil was shot in the chest and later died of his wounds; Al Jazeera correspondent Tareq Abu Azzoum said the boy 'sustained critical injuries, and later, his injuries proved fatal.' In Jabalia, northern Gaza, a man identified as Mohsen Ahmed Bahjat was shot in the head by an Israeli drone. In the Bureij refugee camp, central Gaza, 31-year-old Fidaa Toutah was shot in the head by Israeli tank fire while returning home after dropping her children at school; Abu Azzoum said 'she was preparing her kids for school and went to deliver them to school. On her way back, she was shot by Israeli forces.' A separate drone strike killed one more Palestinian man in Khan Younis city center. Gaza's Health Ministry said Israeli forces had violated the ceasefire for the 346th consecutive day, putting the toll since the ceasefire took effect on October 11, 2025 at 1,394 killed and 4,839 wounded (831 bodies recovered from rubble), and the cumulative toll since October 7, 2023 at 73,914+ killed and 174,935+ wounded. IMEMC separately tallied 21 wounded across Gaza in the same 24-hour period, including incidents in Az-Zahra, Rafah and Deir al-Balah. The IDF did not immediately comment on the individual strikes.

media.caption: Mourners cry over a body at a hospital in Gaza City, September 19, 2026 -- file photo illustrating the aftermath of Israeli strikes on Gaza
media.source: Al Jazeera / Yousef Al Zanoun / AP

confidenceReason: Deaths and named victims corroborated by Al Jazeera correspondent reporting and IMEMC, with cumulative and post-ceasefire toll figures sourced to Gaza's Health Ministry (Tier 1); the Health Ministry and IMEMC figures for the 24-hour death count differ slightly (3 vs 4), a discrepancy typical of same-day Gaza casualty reporting that later reconciles.
